slides.title: Your body *reacts first.*
slides.sub: What the brain does when something feels like a threat.

slides.title: The alarm
slides.body: When the amygdala senses danger, it signals the hypothalamus, which acts like a command center and gears the body up.

slides.title: Before you think
slides.body: It can start before the brain has fully processed what's happening. It's how you jump back from a car before deciding to.

slides.title: Notice it in yourself
slides.body: In a tense moment, what does your body do before you've decided anything? Tight jaw? Hot face? Fast talking?

slides.title: Try this next time
slides.body: Name the signal. Take a few slow breaths from the belly. Then decide what you want to say.
